request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
Sheets in the same tree now share one number sequence: a claim opened on any of them gets the next number after the last one given anywhere in the tree. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The whole change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/SheetRepository.java`:

- **Which sheets count as the tree:** a new `tree(id)` method goes up the parent links to the topmost ancestor that exists, then collects every sheet below it.
- **How the number is taken:** `nextClaimNumber` finds the highest last number across those sheets, adds one, and records that new number on every sheet in the tree. It does this in one statement, so two claims opened at the same moment can't get the same number.
- **What doesn't change:** numbers already given stay as they are, and per-period numbering (`P1-1` and so on) still counts per sheet.

I didn't need to change the database schema or the front end.

**Decision for you:** I count sibling sheets (two sheets with the same parent) as part of the same tree. The tests never put claims on siblings. The existing check that stops a name being reused across a tree uses a narrower tree, without siblings. If you want numbering to use that narrower tree too, it's a small change.

Because every sheet's counter is moved on together, a sheet that later leaves the tree keeps the high number. It won't hand out a number that was already used elsewhere in the tree.
